evidence_summary: Slit2/Robo2 binding and receptor-specific axon-guidance dependence are shown in mouse primary studies; an independent vascular study also requires Robo1/2 for Slit2 responses.
limitations: Heparan-sulfate presentation is a required cofactor and the studies include Robo1 as a parallel receptor; the Slit2-Robo2 pair itself is directly tested.

species_context: human/recombinant and neuronal primary studies; PTP splice context retained
evidence_summary: Primary Slitrk1/PTPσ adhesion and synaptogenic assays support the pair, with independent LAR-RPTP experiments showing PTPσ-specific dependence for Slitrk1 synaptogenic activity.
limitations: PTPσ splice context and synapse type matter; the related PTPδ structure is not being used as the sole evidence.

evidence_summary: Mouse AMH responses require Amhr2 and Bmpr1b; knockdown of either receptor component reduces the response, corroborating earlier AMH/BMPR1B-Smad signaling.
limitations: Developmental/gonadal and GnRH-migration contexts; receptor complex is explicitly preserved as AMHR2 plus BMPR1B.

evidence_summary: AREG is directly evaluated in EGFR/ERBB2 heterodimers with ligand binding and signaling kinetics, and an independent primary study confirms AREG-driven EGFR/ERBB2 signaling in organoid and mouse fibroblast contexts.
limitations: ERBB2 is an obligate heterodimer partner rather than the principal AREG-binding subunit; complex notation is retained.

evidence_summary: BMP10 engages ALK1 with ActRIIA-containing type-II receptor complexes in primary binding/kinetic studies; independent receptor-dosage experiments resolve ACVR2A participation in BMP9/10 signaling.
limitations: BMP10 receptor assembly is multicomponent and endothelial/vascular-context enriched; the preserved complex is ALK1/ACVR2A.

evidence_summary: Primary structural work directly resolves BMP10 with BMPR2, while independent ALK1/type-II receptor studies support the BMP10-ALK1-BMPR2 signaling complex.
limitations: Type-II receptor exchange and receptor abundance affect affinity; BMPR2 is explicitly retained in the complex.

evidence_summary: Human mesenchymal-stromal-cell receptor-utilization experiments support BMP2 signaling through BMPR1A with ACVR2A, corroborated by direct BMP/type-I/type-II interaction measurements.
limitations: Receptor-complex signaling is cell-context dependent and requires a type-II partner; the candidate preserves BMPR1A/ACVR2A.

evidence_summary: A primary BMP2-BMPR1A-ActRIIB ternary structure and mutational analysis directly support the preserved complex; independent biophysical measurements corroborate BMP2/type-II engagement.
limitations: The type-II contribution is lower-affinity and cooperative assembly is not universal; complex is retained explicitly.

evidence_summary: Primary receptor-binding and transcriptional-response work supports BMP2 with BMPR1A and BMPR-II, with independent BLI measurements confirming the pairwise interaction framework.
limitations: BMP2 signaling requires type-I/type-II assembly and receptor abundance can alter apparent usage; preserved complex is BMPR1A/BMPR2.

evidence_summary: Human stromal-cell receptor utilization supports BMP4 through BMPR1A and ACVR2A; independent direct interaction measurements cover BMP4 binding to the relevant receptor classes.
limitations: Cellular usage is context dependent and the receptor complex requires both receptor classes; preserved complex is BMPR1A/ACVR2A.

evidence_summary: Human stromal-cell experiments support BMP4/BMPR1A/BMPR2 receptor utilization, corroborated by direct BMP4 receptor interaction measurements.
limitations: Type-II receptor abundance and cell context affect signaling; preserved complex is BMPR1A/BMPR2.

evidence_summary: Primary BMP6 receptor-binding and functional inhibition studies support ALK2/ACVR1 with BMPR-II, with independent knockdown/inhibition of the same receptor classes reducing BMP6 responses.
limitations: BMP6 also uses alternate type-I receptors and type-II receptor naming differs across studies; ACVR1/BMPR2 is the preserved complex.

evidence_summary: BMP6 primary binding studies detect BMPR1A/BMPR-II usage, and independent receptor-loss experiments confirm BMPR-II-dependent BMP6 signaling with type-I receptor contributions.
limitations: This is a lower-preference BMP6 receptor combination than ALK2/ALK3 in some systems; complex is preserved and not generalized to all BMP6 contexts.

evidence_summary: BTC is directly tested in EGFR/ERBB2 heterodimers and independently shown to activate EGFR with ERBB2 as the preferred heterodimerization partner.
limitations: EGFR is the ligand-binding/activation entry point; ERBB2 is an auxiliary heterodimer partner and the complex is explicitly preserved.

evidence_summary: Primary soluble-receptor studies support BTC activity in ERBB2/ERBB4 combinations, corroborated by independent BTC-induced ErbB2 heterodimerization/activation experiments.
limitations: Direct BTC affinity is strongest through ErbB4/EGFR and ERBB2 is an auxiliary partner; the preserved complex is ERBB2/ERBB4.

species_context: human and/or mouse chemokine studies; orthology noted where limiting
evidence_summary: Primary mutational/binding work maps the CCL3-MIP-1α interaction site on CCR1, corroborated by independent NMR and receptor-binding analyses of the CCL3/CCR1 complex.
limitations: Most pair-specific binding work is human; mouse orthology and chemokine presentation context should remain explicit.

evidence_summary: EGF binding and dimerization are directly quantified for EGFR/ERBB2, with independent structural/functional analysis of EGF-bound EGFR/HER2 complexes.
limitations: EGFR is the primary EGF-binding receptor and ERBB2 modifies dimer affinity/signaling; complex is retained.

evidence_summary: EREG activates pan-ErbB complexes in primary engineered-cell assays, and an independent NSCLC study shows EREG-induced EGFR/ERBB2 heterodimer signaling with ERBB2-dependent AKT output.
limitations: EREG has direct affinity for EGFR/ErbB4 more clearly than isolated ErbB2; EGFR/ERBB2 is retained as a functional heterodimer.

evidence_summary: Primary pan-ErbB ligand studies support EREG activation of ERBB2/ERBB4 combinations, corroborated by independent soluble-receptor binding measurements for the same receptor combination.
limitations: ErbB4 is the principal direct EREG-binding subunit and ERBB2 is an auxiliary partner; complex is explicitly preserved.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: FGF1-FGFR2b binding is directly resolved by structure and mutational analysis, corroborated by a comprehensive primary FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: FGFR2 splice form is essential: evidence is for FGFR2b/FGFR2 ectodomain rather than an undifferentiated receptor isoform.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Direct binding/mutational analysis tests FGF1 with FGFR3, corroborated by the primary mammalian FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: Evidence is splice-form/ectodomain dependent and FGF1 is promiscuous; the FGFR3 receptor form must remain preserved in downstream interpretation.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: FGF10-FGFR2b structure/function studies directly resolve the pair, with an independent mouse/human functional study confirming the FGF10-FGFR2 axis.
limitations: FGFR2b is the relevant splice form and heparan sulfate is required for productive signaling.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary FGF2-FGFR1 complex structural work directly supports the pair, corroborated by a comprehensive receptor-specific FGF panel.
limitations: FGFR1c and heparan sulfate are the relevant molecular context; FGF2 also binds other FGFRs.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary FGF2-FGFR2 complex structural work directly supports the pair, corroborated by a comprehensive receptor-specific FGF panel.
limitations: FGFR2c and heparan sulfate are the relevant molecular context; receptor isoform must remain explicit.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary receptor-specific binding/mutational studies support FGF2-FGFR3c, corroborated by the comprehensive FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: Evidence is strongest for FGFR3c and heparan sulfate-dependent signaling; FGF2 is not receptor-exclusive.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary binding and autophosphorylation experiments identify FGFR4 as a direct FGF2-binding/signaling receptor, corroborated by the complete FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: FGFR4 activity is context and assay dependent and requires heparan sulfate; no splice suffix is needed for this receptor.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary binding/activation and receptor-site mapping support FGF4 with FGFR1 IIIc, corroborated by the comprehensive FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: The direct evidence is for FGFR1c/IIIc and heparan sulfate-dependent signaling; do not generalize to FGFR1b.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary binding/activation and receptor-site mapping support FGF4 with FGFR2 IIIc, corroborated by the comprehensive FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: The direct evidence is for FGFR2c/IIIc and heparan sulfate-dependent signaling; do not generalize to FGFR2b.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary binding/activation and receptor-site mapping support FGF4 with FGFR3 IIIc, corroborated by the comprehensive FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: The direct evidence is for FGFR3c/IIIc and heparan sulfate-dependent signaling.

species_context: human/recombinant and/or mouse/human functional; FGFR splice form retained
evidence_summary: Primary quantitative binding work directly resolves FGF7-FGFR2b, corroborated by the comprehensive FGF-FGFR specificity panel.
limitations: FGFR2b is essential; FGF7-family ligands are splice-form selective and require heparan sulfate.

species_context: human subtype binding and/or mouse type-I IFN response; subtype caveat retained
evidence_summary: IFN-β forms a stable IFNAR1/IFNAR2 receptor complex in primary biochemical studies, corroborated by mouse loss of Ifnar1 eliminating type-I interferon responses.
limitations: The register’s Ifnab label covers the beta subtype; receptor signaling is species and subtype dependent.

species_context: human subtype binding and/or mouse type-I IFN response; subtype caveat retained
evidence_summary: Recombinant IFN-ε binds IFNAR1 and IFNAR2 and activates canonical interferon responses in primary studies; independent mouse protection work confirms IFN-ε biology.
limitations: The protection study reports activity in an Ifnar1-deficient setting, so in-vivo receptor dependence is not clean; promotion rests on direct IFNAR1/2 binding and canonical signaling, not that model.

species_context: human/recombinant and neuronal primary studies; PTP splice context retained
evidence_summary: Primary structural, adhesion, and synaptogenic experiments directly support Slitrk1-PTPδ, with an independent LAR-RPTP study resolving PTPδ-dependent synapse formation.
limitations: PTPδ splice insert meB is required for the best-supported interaction and synaptic phenotype.

species_context: human/recombinant and neuronal primary studies; PTP splice context retained
evidence_summary: Primary crystal/SPR/mutational and synaptogenic studies directly support Slitrk2-PTPδ, corroborated by independent PTPδ-dependent synapse-formation experiments.
limitations: PTPδ splice insert meB and synapse-type context are required; preserve the splice-form limit.

evidence_summary: Primary FZD6-specific signaling and receptor-mobility studies support WNT5A-FZD6 interaction and downstream ERK/DVL behavior.
limitations: WNT5A-FZD6 signaling depends on receptor presentation and Dishevelled/co-receptor context; no isolated high-resolution complex is claimed.

evidence_summary: Primary contactin/Notch work identifies CNTN1 as a functional Notch ligand, and an independent epithelial study supports a CNTN1-Notch2 axis with receptor-specific inhibition.
limitations: This is an atypical contact-mediated Notch interaction rather than a canonical DSL ligand; exosomal/epithelial context is retained.

species_context: linked mouse IL-1-responsive systems; independent human IL-1 receptor cell corroboration
module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal/relay edge with exact kinase identities
evidence_summary: Linked IL-1 perturbations place IRAK in the required MyD88 relay and show IRAK4-dependent recruitment/IRAK1 phosphorylation boundaries. Independent PMID 11960013 reports IRAK4 interaction with IRAK1 and TRAF6, IRAK4-mediated IRAK1 phosphorylation, and dominant-negative IRAK4 blockade of IL-1-induced IRAK1 activation; PMID 28512203 independently supports IRAK4-dependent IRAK1 activation.
limitations: The papers support an IRAK4-to-IRAK1 relay but do not define every phosphorylation site or prove that receptor recruitment is exclusively ordered through IRAK4.

species_context: linked mouse IL-1-responsive systems; independent human IL-1 receptor cell corroboration
module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal/relay edge with exact adaptor identities
evidence_summary: Linked PMID 11518704 shows phosphorylated IRAK associates with membrane, recruits/translocates TRAF6 and assembles the TRAF6-TAK1-TAB1-TAB2 complex. Independent PMID 8837778 shows IL-1-dependent association of TRAF6 with IRAK recruited to the IL-1 receptor.
limitations: This is a recruitment/translocation edge rather than a claim of direct TRAF6 enzymatic activation; isoform and adaptor-complex stoichiometry remain context dependent.

species_context: linked mouse IL-1-responsive systems; independent human IL-1 receptor cell corroboration
module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal/relay edge with exact MAP3K7 identity
evidence_summary: Linked PMID 11518704 connects TRAF6/TAB2 translocation to TAK1 activation. Independent PMID 10882101 identifies TAB2 as the adaptor linking TAK1 to TRAF6 and shows IL-1-induced TAK1-TRAF6 association; PMID 28507161 confirms TRAF6-dependent TAK1 activation under altered TAB2/TAB3 conditions.
limitations: TAB2/TAB3 can provide alternative TAK1 activation routes, so the promotion is for the TRAF6-linked relay and not an assertion that TAB2 is universally required.

species_context: human synthetic/heterologous type-III receptor systems in both studies
module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal relay with exact receptor pair and TYK2 perturbation
evidence_summary: Linked PMID 37725008 uses type-III receptor reconstitution and TYK2 deletion to show a defined TYK2 contribution to IFN-lambda-induced STAT activation. Independent PMID 23830819 shows IFNLR1/IL10RB receptor pairing and proximity to JAK1/TYK2 are required for type-III receptor activity.
limitations: The evidence is synthetic/heterologous and does not establish universal native TYK2 necessity in astrocytes; keep IFN-lambda separate from IFNAR and IFNGR branches.

module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal relay with exact receptor/adaptor identities
evidence_summary: Linked PMID 7544915 shows TRAF2 sufficiency and dominant-negative TRAF2 inhibition of TNFR2-mediated NF-kappaB activation. Independent PMID 25152365 maps TRAF2 binding sites in the TNFR2 intracellular region and the functional NF-kappaB consequence; PMID 11112773 independently supports TNFR2-region recruitment of TRAF2 and NF-kappaB reporter activation.
limitations: TNFR2 also has TRAF2-independent JNK activity and TRAF1/TRAF3 modulation; promotion is limited to the TRAF2-dependent NF-kappaB relay and not all TNFR2 outputs.

species_context: linked Xenopus laevis developmental retinal neurons; independent mammalian mouse cortical-neuron and biochemical corroboration
module_fit: 21A receptor-proximal noncanonical relay with exact receptor-tail/kinase identities
evidence_summary: Linked PMID 19361494 shows deletion of the BMPR2 LIMK1-binding region impairs BMP-dependent retinal axon extension. Independent PMID 15538389 demonstrates BMPRII-LIMK1 binding, BMP7-dependent dendritic effects, LIMK1 catalytic activation and loss of function after disrupting the receptor-tail interaction.
limitations: The exact SCI receiver context and BMP7-specific ligand assignment remain unresolved; promotion is for the BMPR2-LIMK1 edge, not a general BMP receptor or injury claim.

evidence_summary: Laminin-332 perturbation and alpha3beta1 blockade resolve a matrix-to-integrin focal-adhesion relay with FAK/SRC readouts.
limitations: Carcinoma mechanistic anchor; gamma2-containing laminin matrix was perturbed as a complex rather than isolated LAMA3.

evidence_summary: Laminin-332 matrix adhesion and alpha6beta4-dependent hemidesmosome organization are resolved at the integrin-complex level.
limitations: Matrix organization and hemidesmosome assays are context-dependent; no SCI model.

evidence_summary: Recombinant laminin-411 shows alpha6beta1 binding, corroborated by laminin-411/421 alpha6beta1 adhesion and vascular-laminin assays.
limitations: Binding is modest and comparator-cell based; retain the complete alpha6beta1 heterodimer.

evidence_summary: The TNC TNfn3/RGD domain supports resolved alpha8beta1 binding and adhesion in recombinant and cell-based assays.
limitations: Evidence is strongest for the defined TNC fragment/domain, not unrestricted full-length TNC.

evidence_summary: TNC binding and alphaVbeta6 assignment are supported by TNC-agarose/neutralization and independent epithelial TNC-alphaVbeta6 adhesion context.
limitations: No purified affinity measurement; cellular matrix context and complete alphaVbeta6 are required.

evidence_summary: ICAM1 engagement of LFA1 resolves an adhesion-to-Src/Rap1-actin/Pyk2 relay across independent primary studies.
limitations: LFA1 is the complete alphaLbeta2 heterodimer; relay is receptor-proximal and not a terminal TF.

evidence_summary: ICAM1 is recognized by the Mac1 alphaMbeta2 I-domain/heterodimer in direct binding and leukocyte-adhesion assays.
limitations: Preserve the complete Mac1 complex; avoid interpreting this as free ITGAM or ITGB2 binding.

evidence_summary: VCAM1 directly supports alpha9beta1 adhesion, with an independent alpha9-dependent VCAM1/FAK-Src-ERK chemotaxis study.
limitations: Complete alpha9beta1 is required; comparator/non-SCI context limits injury-specific inference.

evidence_summary: VCAM1-alpha9beta1 engagement is linked to FAK/Src/ERK chemotaxis, corroborated by direct alpha9beta1 adhesion evidence.
limitations: This is an adhesion relay rather than a terminal TF; retain alpha9beta1 complex context.

evidence_summary: Thy-1 engages the alphaVbeta3-syndecan-4 adhesion complex in cell-contact assays, with FAK/PKCalpha/RhoA/PI3K/Rac1 outputs.
limitations: Three-component contact complex and cell presentation are required; do not collapse to alphaVbeta3 alone.

evidence_summary: Thy-1 cell-cell contact through alphaVbeta3/SDC4 produces a resolved FAK/PI3K/Rac1/RhoA adhesion relay.
limitations: Relay is complex-dependent and not a terminal transcriptional readout.

evidence_summary: MAdCAM1 is a direct ligand for the alpha4beta7 adhesion receptor, with independent homing/adhesion and receptor-specific evidence.
limitations: Complete alpha4beta7 heterodimer and endothelial addressin presentation are required.

evidence_summary: MAdCAM1-alpha4beta7 engagement produces paxillin/Cas-L and homing-associated adhesion signaling, anchored by direct receptor evidence.
limitations: Proximal adhesion relay; no terminal TF and no SCI-specific model.

evidence_summary: NCAM1 homophilic engagement is supported by independent neurite/adhesion studies and resolves a Src/FAK neurite relay.
limitations: Homophilic NCAM1 presentation and neural context are required; not an ECM ligand.

evidence_summary: Nephronectin/NPNT binds alpha8beta1 and drives defined adhesion through the RGD/FEI matrix interface.
limitations: Matrix domain and complete alpha8beta1 context must be retained.

evidence_summary: Netrin-1 directly binds neogenin in structural/biophysical work and is independently confirmed within a resolved NEO1 guidance-cue complex.
limitations: Netrin family and co-receptor context must not be conflated; this row is specifically NTN1-NEO1.

evidence_summary: Podoplanin engages CLEC-2 through defined glycan/protein contacts and receptor clustering, supported by direct structure and signaling studies.
limitations: Glycosylation and receptor clustering are required; this is a platelet/immune adhesion context.

evidence_summary: Podoplanin-CLEC-2 engagement activates the resolved Src-Syk-LAT-PLCgamma2 hemITAM relay.
limitations: Relay depends on CLEC-2 clustering and cellular presentation; not a terminal TF.

evidence_summary: Pleiotrophin supports a resolved alphaVbeta3/PTPRZ1 adhesion branch, corroborated by independent PTN/PTPRZ1/alphaVbeta3 migration signaling.
limitations: PTN receptor branches are context-dependent; preserve the alphaVbeta3/PTPRZ1 co-receptor configuration.

evidence_summary: PTN binds and inhibits PTPRZ1 phosphatase activity in independent primary studies, resolving the ligand-to-receptor branch.
limitations: PTN/PTPRZ1 is a phosphatase-receptor context rather than a classical integrin; downstream effects are cell-state dependent.

evidence_summary: PTN/HB-GAM binds syndecan-3 and supports Src/cortactin-associated adhesion signaling in independent neural/osteoblast systems.
limitations: Proteoglycan glycosaminoglycan/core-protein presentation is required; preserve SDC3 specificity.

evidence_summary: Reelin directly engages ApoER2/LRP8 in binding, clustering, and Dab1/Src/Akt studies.
limitations: Reelin is a large extracellular glycoprotein and receptor clustering/context are required.

evidence_summary: Reelin directly engages VLDLR in receptor-binding and clustering studies with independent downstream signaling support.
limitations: Reelin receptor clustering and extracellular presentation are required; do not merge with LRP8.

evidence_summary: RGMA-NEO1 binding and receptor-proximal guidance branches are supported across multiple independent primary studies.
limitations: RGMA has parallel receptor/co-receptor branches; this row is specifically NEO1.

evidence_summary: Syndecan-2 association with PTPRJ/CD148 is supported by independent primary studies and linked to integrin/Src adhesion signaling.
limitations: Association is context-dependent and does not imply a freely soluble binary ligand.

evidence_summary: E-selectin recognizes the GLG1/ESL-1 glycan-bearing adhesion receptor in direct rolling/adhesion studies.
limitations: Glycan presentation and endothelial rolling context are required.

evidence_summary: Sema3A forms the defined neuropilin-1/plexin-A1 receptor complex with receptor-proximal guidance signaling.
limitations: Preserve the NRP1:PLXNA1 complex; semaphorin receptor composition is not interchangeable across plexins.

evidence_summary: Sema3G engages the defined NRP2:plexin-A1 complex in primary receptor/functional studies.
limitations: Complex composition is critical; related Sema3G/NRP2/Plexin-D1 evidence is not substituted for Plexin-A1.

evidence_summary: Sema7A binds and signals through the alpha1beta1 integrin in direct/functional primary studies.
limitations: Complete alpha1beta1 and glycosylated membrane presentation are required.

evidence_summary: SPP1/osteopontin engages CD44 variant isoforms in direct adhesion/signaling studies.
limitations: CD44 variant and glycosylation context matter; do not generalize to all CD44 forms.

evidence_summary: TGM2 associates with syndecan-4 and supports defined adhesion/FAK-linked signaling across independent studies.
limitations: Matrix crosslinking and SDC4 presentation are context-dependent; no purified binary affinity was required for this adhesion-complex promotion.

evidence_summary: The versican G3 domain supports a defined beta1-integrin interface and adhesion/FAK signaling, with independent rat ECM-interface evidence.
limitations: Promotion is domain/isoform-specific; do not generalize G3 evidence to all versican forms or infer a single alpha partner.

evidence_summary: EFNA1-EPHA4 binding and EphA4-proximal cytoskeletal/adhesion signaling are supported by receptor-selectivity and independent monocyte/neural studies.
limitations: Ephrin ligand presentation and receptor clustering are required; no SCI-specific validation.

evidence_summary: EFNA2 binds EPHA7 in direct receptor-selectivity work and independent neural signaling studies.
limitations: EphA7 isoform/processing and membrane presentation matter; no SCI-specific validation.

exact_evidence_status: exact ATP-P2X7R agonist-receptor edge at pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: Rat impact SCI shows sustained extracellular ATP, ATP-evoked calcium injury, and OxATP or PPADS protection; independent SCI and spinal-slice studies support ATP-gated P2X7 pharmacology.
limitations: OxATP, PPADS, and BBG have selectivity limits; pharmacology does not establish purified binding or exclude contributions from other ATP receptors.

exact_evidence_status: exact ATP-P2X4R agonist-receptor edge at pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: SCI ATP-evoked calcium and P2X4-associated pain signaling are supported by an independent SCI study showing excess ATP and P2X4 inhibition reduce neuropathic pain.
limitations: Evidence is pharmacologic rather than purified binding; P2X4 selectivity and ATP receptor-family contributions remain bounded.

exact_evidence_status: exact CXCL10-CXCR3 chemokine-GPCR edge; receptor-proximal function
evidence_summary: Recombinant CXCL10 and CXCR3 antagonist AMD487 altered glial activation and inflammatory pain after spinal ischemia-reperfusion; independent CCI studies reproduce CXCL10-CXCR3 pharmacology with AMG487 or anti-CXCL10.
limitations: No purified binding; most SCI corroboration is ischemia-reperfusion or CCI rather than contusion; antagonist specificity remains a limitation.

exact_evidence_status: exact CXCL3-CXCR2 chemokine-GPCR edge; receptor-proximal function
evidence_summary: Mouse traumatic SCI CXCL3 administration and CXCR2 inhibition link the pair to macrophage-fibroblast scar signaling; independent CINC-3/CXCL3 receptor pharmacology shows CXCR2-dependent chemotaxis and calcium responses.
limitations: No purified binding; CXCR2 inhibitor specificity and administration route limit causal interpretation; scar output remains downstream of the receptor edge.

exact_evidence_status: exact bradykinin-BDKRB2 edge at receptor-proximal pharmacologic level
evidence_summary: Neonatal mouse spinal preparation and microglia assays support bradykinin/B2R effects; independent rat spinal ischemia and spinal-slice antagonist studies support B2R-dependent bradykinin responses.
limitations: Primary spinal study is neonatal and not adult lesion-core tissue; receptor assignment is pharmacologic and no purified bradykinin-B2R binding or endogenous lesion release was shown.

exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-GlcNAc-P2Y14 molecular edge; no SCI-context claim
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 or neutrophil studies show UDP-N-acetylglucosamine activation of Gi/Rho and chemotaxis, with independent pharmacology and newer structure-function work reproducing receptor-specific activity.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no endogenous SCI release or lesion-context evidence; efficacy and partial agonism vary by cell state and assay.

exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-galactose-P2Y14 molecular edge; no SCI-context claim
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 or neutrophil studies show UDP-galactose-associated Gi/Rho signaling, independently reproduced by receptor-structure/function and cell-death release studies.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no endogenous SCI release; receptor efficacy is cell-state-dependent and the ligand can show partial activity in native cells.

exact_evidence_status: exact UDP-glucuronic-acid-P2Y14 molecular edge; assay-dependent efficacy
evidence_summary: Recombinant P2Y14 and differentiated HL60 assays support UDP-glucuronic acid receptor activity, with independent human neutrophil and newer structure-function studies testing the same ligand-receptor edge.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no SCI release evidence; activity is weaker or partial in native neutrophils and depends on cell state.

exact_evidence_status: exact PGE2-EP4 prostanoid-GPCR edge; receptor branch separated from EP2
evidence_summary: PGE2-EP4 activity is supported in primary spinal cultures and by independent recombinant EP4 binding, desensitization, structural, and myeloid functional studies.
limitations: High confidence is the molecular/receptor branch; EP2 and other prostanoid receptors remain separate; the primary SCI evidence is spinal culture or neuroinflammation rather than contusion.

exact_evidence_status: exact resistin-TLR4/MD2 complex edge; receptor-proximal signaling
evidence_summary: Primary human or mouse TLR4 reconstitution and blockade studies support resistin-TLR4/MD2 inflammatory signaling; independent central binding and macrophage studies reproduce TLR4-dependent resistin effects.
limitations: High confidence is a molecular complex edge, not SCI evidence; TLR4/MD2 context and tissue-specific resistin biology remain limitations.

exact_evidence_status: exact FLRT3-FLRT3 homophilic adhesion edge; not a downstream signaling claim
evidence_summary: FLRT3 LRR interface mutants and full-length aggregation support FLRT3-FLRT3 homophilic adhesion, with independent developmental studies showing FLRT3-family homophilic contact localization.
limitations: This promotes a molecular adhesion edge only; some studies find no soluble or trans homophilic binding, and heterophilic FLRT3-ADGRL3/UNC5 edges must remain separate from adhesion and SCI function.

evidence_summary: GHSR-null specificity and ghrelin-challenge experiments establish LEAP2 antagonism; independent discovery and fluorescent-LEAP2 studies show GHSR binding, antagonism, and inverse agonism.
limitations: High confidence is molecular/pharmacologic; no SCI evidence and the evidence is not a purified structural binding assay.

exact_evidence_status: exact SAA1-TLR4/MD2 complex edge with direct binding and independent microglia confirmation
evidence_summary: SPR/co-IP and TLR4 or MD2 perturbation support direct SAA1-TLR4/MD2 engagement; an independent 2026 primary microglia study confirms biochemical interaction and TLR4/MD2-dependent inflammatory activation.
limitations: High confidence is the TLR4/MD2 complex edge; no SCI model; SAA1 receptor usage is context-dependent and the microglia study uses pharmacologic MD2/TLR4 perturbation.

exact_evidence_status: exact mouse SAA3-fragment-MD2/TLR4 complex edge; fragment boundary explicit
evidence_summary: Synthetic SAA3(20-86) and (43-57) peptides show direct SPR binding to purified TLR4/MD2 and MD2-dependent signaling; an independent premetastatic primary study assigns TLR4 as a functional receptor for SAA3.
limitations: Promoted only for the defined mouse SAA3 peptide/MD2-TLR4 edge; not full-length human SAA3; no SCI model; downstream p38/NFkB remains separate.

exact_evidence_status: exact VCAN-TLR2:TLR6/CD14 complex edge; not a binary VCAN-TLR2 claim
evidence_summary: Primary biochemical and cell studies identify a TLR2/TLR6/CD14 complex for VCAN inflammatory activity; an independent 2025 primary study reproduces VCAN-TLR2-MyD88 inflammatory signaling.
limitations: Promoted at the complex level only; no purified binary VCAN-TLR2 binding, no SCI model, and downstream macrophage polarization remains distinct.

evidence_summary: Primary chemotaxis and recruitment studies support CCL27-CCR10, independently reproduced by the original orphan-receptor binding report and newer receptor selectivity/structure-function work.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; no SCI model; skin-homing context and chemokine glycosaminoglycan presentation remain separate from the exact receptor edge.

exact_evidence_status: exact CCL28-CCR3 chemokine-GPCR edge; dual-receptor usage retained
evidence_summary: Primary CCL28-CCR3 comparator pharmacology is independently supported by receptor-selectivity and structural work distinguishing CCR3 from the shared CCR10 branch.
limitations: High confidence is the exact CCR3 edge, not exclusive receptor usage; CCL28-CCR10 remains separate; no SCI model.

evidence_summary: Primary receptor pharmacology and a later two-site CCR1 binding/activation study identify CCL7 as a cognate CCR1 ligand; independent MCP chemokine work supports receptor-proximal signaling.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; CCL7 is promiscuous across chemokine receptors and no SCI receptor-causal validation was located.

evidence_summary: Primary CCL7/MCP-3 receptor pharmacology plus independent MCP-3 chemotaxis and CCR2B-transfectant signaling studies support the exact CCR2B edge.
limitations: High confidence is molecular only; CCL7 is multi-receptor and no SCI receptor-causal validation was located; retain CCR1/CCR3 edges separately.
